note.question: Can a matching platform's self-imposed ticket price cap raise its own commission revenue, and when does doing so paradoxically increase average prices or harm buyers?
note.overview: The paper solves a multistage matching-platform game in which the platform chooses a price cap, heterogeneous sellers decide participation and prices, and buyers strategically direct their search while anticipating congestion and rationing.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The platform first chooses a cap C. Sellers then decide whether to remain on the platform. Participating sellers simultaneously post prices no greater than C. Buyers observe prices and randomize over at most one seller so that expected market utility is equalized across visited seller types; if several buyers visit the same seller, the single ticket is randomly rationed.
